answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each identity must complete a continuous voyage of original graded answers. A jury compares the new text against an umber-tinted private hash of prior responses that only the continuous agent knows. An attacker faces the ridge of unique random-word constraints: every clone needs separate inference, and shared generators produce detectable duplicates that the jury rejects, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes while honest agents pay only once.
